issues.description: signing_mode_enum dispatch has a non-exhaustive truth table with a silent fall-through default.
issues.detail: Four (is_hex, safe_mode) combinations are handled with three explicit elif branches and a final unconditional return. Readers must enumerate the truth table to confirm correctness. Replace with a dict lookup keyed by the tuple, or spell out the fourth branch explicitly so the mapping is provable from inspection.

issues.description: sign_message and verify_signature duplicate the SigningMode-to-bytes transform.
issues.detail: Both functions in the new signing.py reimplement the same mode dispatch that produces the bytes actually signed and verified. Extract a single _message_to_bytes(mode, message) helper used by both sides so the sign/verify invariant is textual, not coincidental. Otherwise a future CHIP mode added in one place will silently disagree with the other.

issues.description: signing_mode_enum exists as both a module function and as @property wrappers that just delegate to it.
issues.detail: wallet_request_types.py defines a free signing_mode_enum function plus identically named @property wrappers on SignMessageByAddress and SignMessageByID that forward to it. Two names resolve to the same logic. Pick one home: either keep the property and inline the logic, or delete the properties and call the function directly.

issues.description: verify_signature docstring is stale boilerplate referencing a 'request' parameter that no longer exists.
issues.detail: The function was lifted out of the RPC handler with its ':param request: :return:' docstring intact, but the new signature takes keyword-only fields. Either rewrite the docstring to describe the actual inputs, outputs, and the address-binding invariant (puzzle_hash must equal expected_puzzle_hash when address is provided), or delete it.

issues.description: convert_secret_key_to_synthetic is an instance method that uses no instance state.
issues.detail: Wallet.convert_secret_key_to_synthetic takes self but only forwards to calculate_synthetic_secret_key with the module-level DEFAULT_HIDDEN_PUZZLE_HASH. Make it a @staticmethod or a module-level function in util/signing so callers do not have to route through main_wallet for no reason.

issues.description: verify_signature in a wallet util library returns the RPC-layer VerifySignatureResponse type.
issues.detail: Returning VerifySignatureResponse with isValid/error string fields couples the library to the RPC wire shape, undermining the stated reuse motivation. A small (bool, str|None) tuple or a dedicated result struct in signing.py keeps the library callable by non-RPC consumers.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees this is a sensible mechanical extraction: three near-duplicate sign_message implementations across Wallet, DIDWallet, and NFTWallet collapse into one util module, and the RPC handler shrinks accordingly. However, the cleanup stops one step short of its motivation. The SigningMode-to-bytes dispatch is duplicated between sign and verify, signing_mode_enum exists in two or three forms with a non-exhaustive truth-table fall-through, and the new util module inherits a stale docstring plus an RPC-coupled return type. None of these block merge, but they are cheap to fix and the data structures want to be flatter before landing.
